How the team uses this
  1. At home: Train on your phone (Listen mode, buzz, 5 seconds), play the Daily Ten, drill Terms and Units.
  2. Practice night: the coach opens Arena on the laptop and turns on phone buzzers. Everyone taps Join a match (or scans the QR code on the board), picks their team and buzzes on their own phone. Laptop keys and touch buttons work too.
  3. Leaderboard: copy your score card from Leaderboard and send it to the coach; the coach pastes the cards and the ranking updates.

In-person practice match

Arena

How a practice match works
  1. Coach: open this page on the laptop or projector, type the team or player names, and choose how people buzz (below).
  2. Phones (easiest): press Turn on phone buzzers. Players scan the QR code, type their name and tap their team. Their phone becomes their buzzer, so nobody shares a keyboard.
  3. No phones? Each name gets its own laptop key, because one keyboard cannot tell people apart. Touch buttons under the board work too. Or tick Coach picks so any key stops the clock and you tap who buzzed.
  4. Press Start match, then space for each question. Players say the answer out loud within 5 seconds and you press Correct Y or Wrong N. A wrong answer passes the question to the others.
Mode
Names and laptop keys
Phone buzzers

Every player buzzes on their own phone. No app, no account. Phones and the laptop both need internet.

Topics
Difficulty
Coach keys: space start or next, Y correct, N wrong, R repeat, T throw out. Official scoring: +10 correct, −5 wrong, buzz any time while the question is read and up to 5 seconds after it ends, two appeals each (tap "Appeals" for a coach review before moving on).

Waiting for the coach…
How phone buzzing works
  1. The coach turns on phone buzzers in the Arena. The board shows a match code and a QR code.
  2. Scan the QR code, or open this app and tap Join a match, then type the code and your name.
  3. Tap your team. When the coach starts a question, your button lights up. Tap it the moment you know the answer, then say the answer out loud.
  4. The board decides who was first, even between phones and laptop keys. A buzz that arrives a moment late still counts if it was pressed first.
  5. Keep this screen open. The phone stays awake while you are in a match.
